# AI-QR-code-scanning-
QR / barcode scanning for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): give the model eyes for codes — from image files,
the live screen, or a webcam — plus QR generation.
Decoding is powered by **zxing-cpp compiled to WebAssembly** (`zxing-wasm`), the same C++ core behin
d most desktop scanners, so rotated, inverted, tiny, perspective-skewed and multi-symbol images all
t desktop scanners, so rotated, inverted, tiny, perspective-skewed and multi-symbol images all work.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does | Input |

| `qr_scan` | Decode every code in an image, with positions | path, glob, http(s) URL |
| `qr_scan_s

creen` | Capture the screen (optionally a region) and decode | `region: "x,y,w,h"` |
| `qr_scan_came

ra` | Grab one webcam frame and decode | optional device name |
| `qr_make` | Render text/URL as a Q
R PNG | writes to `.dsh-qr/` in the workspace |

Restart DeepSeek Harness afterwards. Uninstall with `-Uninstall`.
## Why a plugin instead of a script
On the shared 10-image corpus (rotation, inversion, 78px thumbnail, blurry JPEG, perspective, two co
des in one frame) zxing-cpp scores 10/10 — see `tools/_bench/results.md`. Running it in-process remo
ves the interpreter startup:
| Metric | Python script | This plugin |

| One decode (cold) | ~750 ms | 92 ms (WASM load) |
| One decode (warm) | ~750 ms | **13.6 ms** |
|
Full-screen capture + decode | ~1 500 ms | **227 ms** |

## Privacy
Everything runs locally: WASM decoding, GDI screen capture, ffmpeg frame grabs. No network calls unl
ess you pass an explicit http(s) URL to `qr_scan`. Screenshots stay in memory unless `save: true`.
## Limitations
- Screen capture uses Win32 GDI via `koffi`, so it is **Windows-only**; `qr_scan` and `qr_make` stil

l work elsewhere.
- Webcam capture needs `ffmpeg` on `PATH` (or `DSH_FFMPEG`).
- Image formats: PNG/
JPEG/WebP/GIF/BMP/TIFF/AVIF (decoded by sharp).
